scope: containment of Approximate-KV taint on the CPU reference path: a harness-only stub Approximate producer over a genuine cold prefill of the R005 tiny model, and PtrRuntime's persistent taint registry, derivation hops, Raw admission rule, Pod, SemDB and merge containment over a durable FileLedger; a taint-containment claim only
limitations: the Approximate producer is a pinned stub: the label is the stub's, not a measurement, and no real Approximate producer is tested
the content index matches only the exact digest of a whole segment: a paraphrase, substring, re-tokenisation or whitespace edit of tainted text is not detected
honest text identical to tainted text is tainted too (a false positive, accepted: the runtime fails closed)
the runtime trusts the backend's KV-reuse report; a backend that mislabels an Approximate run as Exact is outside the claim
the Exact-only KV catalog guard is structural (Approximate sessions never look up or insert), not a check inside the catalog
cleared taint leaves tombstones in materialized state; a ledger writer who knows a recipe could forge a Clear (trusted-ledger model, the recompute digest is not verifiable on replay)
the Request subject is never cleared and Pod-side taint records are permanent
model_pin_mismatches and taint_lost are weak metrics (constants and the harness's own record, as the preregistration says)
the code under test is the CPU reference path with a tiny seeded model; no GPU, no large model
timings come from one shared cloud container; no capacity claim
